title: Schema
description: A data-shape definition, expressed as an OpenAPI 3.0 Schema Object, that constrains the type and structure of a value exchanged over the API, such as a request body, response body, parameter or header value. It is either a named entry under components/schemas or an inline schema nested in a media type, parameter, header or another schema. Use MediaType instead when the element is the MIME-type-keyed content entry (e.g. application/json) that wraps a schema together with examples and encoding, rather than the shape definition itself. Use Parameter instead when the element is a named operation input with a location (path, query, header or cookie), whose value type is merely described by a referenced schema. Use Components instead when the element is the registry that holds reusable schemas, responses and parameters, not an individual type definition. Use Example instead when the element is a concrete sample value illustrating data, rather than the constraints the data must satisfy.

type.description: The JSON data type of the value: one of string, number, integer, boolean, array or object. OpenAPI 3.0 does not allow type arrays or 'null'. Set it on every non-$ref, non-composed schema.

title.description: A short human-readable label for the schema, typically the model or DTO name. Set it when documentation tooling should display a name other than the component key.

description.description: Explanatory text for the schema or property, in CommonMark. Set it whenever the meaning of the value is not obvious from its name and type.

format.description: A modifier refining 'type', such as int32, int64, float, double, byte, binary, date, date-time, password, email or uuid. Set it when the base type alone does not convey the value's encoding or semantics.

default.description: The value the server assumes when the consumer omits this property or parameter. It must conform to the schema's type. Set it only when an actual server-side default exists.

enum.description: The closed set of literal values the data may take, each valid against the schema's type, as declared by the enum keyword. Set it for fixed vocabularies such as status codes or modes. This schema stores the set as a single string.

nullable.description: Boolean, default false. When true, null is an accepted value in addition to the declared type (the OpenAPI 3.0 substitute for type: [T, null]). Set it when the API may send or accept explicit nulls.

properties.description: Map of property names to schema definitions for object types

items.description: Schema definition for array element types

required.description: List of required property names for object types

allOf.description: Composed schema: value must be valid against all listed schemas

oneOf.description: Composed schema: value must be valid against exactly one of the listed schemas

anyOf.description: Composed schema: value must be valid against one or more of the listed schemas

$ref.description: JSON Reference to another schema definition. In OpenAPI 3.0, sibling keywords are ignored when $ref is present.

readOnly.description: Indicates the property is read-only and should not be sent in request bodies.

writeOnly.description: Indicates the property is write-only and should not be included in response bodies.

deprecated.description: Marks the schema as deprecated. Consumers should migrate away from using it.

discriminator.description: Adds support for polymorphism by specifying the property name that determines the subtype (propertyName) and an optional mapping of values to schema references.

xml.description: XML serialization metadata for this schema when producing XML representations.

externalDocs.description: Reference to an api.externaldocumentation node providing additional documentation for this schema.

x-dr-evidence: A DTO or model class used as a route's request or response type and annotated for OpenAPI generation, such as a Pydantic model passed as response_model in FastAPI, a NestJS class with @ApiProperty fields, or a Java class with @Schema.
An entry under '#/components/schemas/' or a 'schema:' block beneath 'content' in an openapi.yaml/json file, containing keywords such as type, properties, required, items, allOf or $ref.
A validation schema object attached to a route definition, such as a Fastify route 'schema: { body, response }', a zod/joi schema converted to OpenAPI, or a model class emitted by openapi-generator.
